nodes.summary: Let $t$ be a Fenwick tree over a commutative additive monoid $\alpha$, and let $n$ be its size (the length of its stored array minus one). For every natural number $i \ge n$ and every $\delta \in \alpha$, the point update of $t$ adding $\delta$ at position $i$ returns $t$ itself.
nodes.title: Out-of-range point updates leave a Fenwick tree unchanged

nodes.summary: Let $t$ be a Fenwick tree over a commutative additive monoid $\alpha$, let $n$ be its size (the length of its stored array minus one), let $i$ be a natural number and let $\delta \in \alpha$. Adding $\delta$ at underlying position $i$ adds $\delta$ to the stored entries at the one-indexed positions $j_1 = i + 1$ and $j_{k+1} = j_k + \operatorname{lowbit}(j_k)$, for as long as $j_k \le n$, where…
nodes.title: Point update of a Fenwick tree

nodes.summary: For an array $a$ of elements of a commutative additive monoid $\alpha$ and a natural number $j$, this is the sum of the $\operatorname{lowbit}(j)$ entries of $a$ ending at zero-indexed position $j - 1$, where $\operatorname{lowbit}(j)$ is the largest power of two dividing $j$ (with $\operatorname{lowbit}(0) = 0$) and entries past the end of $a$ count as $0$.
nodes.title: Interval sum read from an array

nodes.summary: For a list $a$ of elements of a commutative additive monoid $\alpha$ and a natural number $j$, the interval sum at the one-indexed position $j$ is the sum of the $\operatorname{lowbit}(j)$ entries of $a$ ending at zero-indexed position $j - 1$, where $\operatorname{lowbit}(j)$ is the largest power of two dividing $j$ (with $\operatorname{lowbit}(0) = 0$) and entries past the end of $a$ count as $0$.
nodes.title: Fenwick-tree interval sum of a list

nodes.summary: For a list $a$ of length $n$ over a commutative additive monoid $\alpha$, the Fenwick tree built from $a$ stores the array of length $n + 1$ whose entry at index $0$ is $0$ and whose entry at each one-indexed position $j$ with $1 \le j \le n$ is the sum of the $\operatorname{lowbit}(j)$ entries of $a$ ending at zero-indexed position $j - 1$, where $\operatorname{lowbit}(j)$ is the largest power of two dividing $j$.
nodes.title: Building a Fenwick tree from a list

nodes.summary: A Fenwick tree (binary indexed tree) over a commutative additive monoid $\alpha$ is an array of elements of $\alpha$, read as one-indexed interval sums with an unused dummy entry at index $0$. The structure itself imposes no condition on the entries, and the underlying array it represents is not stored; the relation saying that a tree represents a given array is defined separately.
nodes.title: Fenwick tree

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n > 0$, the quotient $n / \operatorname{lowbit}(n)$ is odd, where $\operatorname{lowbit}(n)$ is the value of the lowest set bit of $n$ in binary.
nodes.title: Dividing out the lowest set bit leaves an odd number

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n > 0$, $\operatorname{lowbit}(n)$ divides $n$, where $\operatorname{lowbit}(n)$ is the value of the lowest set bit of $n$ in binary.
nodes.title: The lowest set bit divides the number

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n$, $\operatorname{lowbit}(n) \le n$, where $\operatorname{lowbit}(n)$ is the value of the lowest set bit of $n$ in binary (with $\operatorname{lowbit}(0) = 0$).
nodes.title: The lowest set bit is at most the number

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n > 0$, $\operatorname{lowbit}(n) > 0$, where $\operatorname{lowbit}(n)$ is the value of the lowest set bit of $n$ in binary.
nodes.title: The lowest set bit of a positive number is positive

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n > 0$, $\operatorname{lowbit}(n)$ is a power of two: $\operatorname{lowbit}(n) = 2^k$ for some natural number $k$.
nodes.title: The lowest set bit is a power of two

nodes.summary: By convention, $\operatorname{lowbit}(0) = 0$.
nodes.title: Lowbit of zero

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n > 0$, $\operatorname{lowbit}(n)$ is the largest power of two dividing $n$; for $n = 0$ it is defined as $\operatorname{lowbit}(0) = 0$.
nodes.title: Lowest set bit

nodes.summary: Let $t$ be a Fenwick tree representing a list $a$ of elements of an additive commutative monoid, let $i < |a|$ be a position, let $\delta$ be an element of the monoid, and let $k$ be any natural number, possibly larger than $|a|$. Then the prefix sum of length $k$ of the tree obtained from $t$ by adding $\delta$ at position $i$ equals the prefix sum of length $k$ of $t$ plus $\delta$ if $i < k$, and equals the…
nodes.title: Prefix sums after a point update

nodes.summary: For every list $a$ of elements of an additive commutative monoid and every natural number $k$, the prefix sum of length $k$ of the Fenwick tree built from $a$ equals the sum of the first $\min(k, |a|)$ entries of $a$.
nodes.title: Prefix sums of a built Fenwick tree

nodes.summary: Let $t$ be a Fenwick tree representing a list $a$ of elements of an additive commutative monoid. Then for every natural number $k$, including $k > |a|$, the prefix sum of length $k$ of $t$ equals the sum of the first $\min(k, |a|)$ entries of $a$.
nodes.title: Correctness of Fenwick tree prefix sums

nodes.summary: For every Fenwick tree $t$ over an additive commutative monoid, the prefix sum of length $0$ of $t$ is $0$.
nodes.title: The empty prefix sum is zero

nodes.summary: Let $t$ be a Fenwick tree over an additive commutative monoid with $n$ underlying entries, let $k$ be a natural number and let $m = \min(k, n)$. The prefix sum of length $k$ of $t$ is the sum of the stored entries of $t$ at the positions $j_0 = m$, $j_{r+1} = j_r - \operatorname{lowbit}(j_r)$, taken for as long as $j_r > 0$.
nodes.title: Fenwick tree prefix sum

nodes.summary: Let $t$ be a Fenwick tree representing a list $a = (a_0, \dots, a_{n-1})$ of elements of an additive commutative group. Then for all natural numbers $\mathit{lo}$ and $\mathit{hi}$, the range sum of $t$ over $[\mathit{lo}, \mathit{hi})$ equals $\sum_{\mathit{lo} \le i < \min(\mathit{hi}, n)} a_i$; in particular it is $0$ when $\mathit{hi} \le \mathit{lo}$.
nodes.title: Correctness of Fenwick tree range sums

nodes.summary: For a Fenwick tree $t$ over an additive commutative group and natural numbers $\mathit{lo}$ and $\mathit{hi}$, the range sum of $t$ over $[\mathit{lo}, \mathit{hi})$ is $0$ if $\mathit{hi} \le \mathit{lo}$, and otherwise the prefix sum of length $\mathit{hi}$ of $t$ minus the prefix sum of length $\mathit{lo}$ of $t$.
nodes.title: Fenwick tree range sum

nodes.summary: For every list $a$ over an additive commutative monoid, the Fenwick tree built from $a$ has size equal to the length of $a$.
nodes.title: Size of a built Fenwick tree

nodes.summary: If a Fenwick tree $t$ over an additive commutative monoid represents a list $a$, then the size of $t$ equals the length of $a$.
nodes.title: A Fenwick tree has the length of the list it represents

nodes.summary: The size of a Fenwick tree is the length of its stored array minus one, truncated at $0$; the one accounts for the dummy entry at index $0$. It is read off the stored array in constant time.
nodes.title: Size of a Fenwick tree

nodes.summary: Let $t$ be a Fenwick tree over an additive commutative monoid that represents a list $a$ of length $n$. For every index $i < n$ (counting from $0$) and every element $\delta$, the tree obtained from $t$ by adding $\delta$ at position $i$ represents the list obtained from $a$ by replacing its entry $a_i$ with $a_i + \delta$.
nodes.title: Point update preserves representation

nodes.summary: For every list $a$ over an additive commutative monoid, the Fenwick tree built from $a$ represents $a$.
nodes.title: Building a Fenwick tree yields a valid representation

nodes.summary: A Fenwick tree $t$ over an additive commutative monoid represents a list $a$ of length $n$ when its stored array has length $n + 1$ (a dummy entry at index $0$ plus one entry per element of $a$) and, for every $j$ with $1 \le j \le n$, the stored entry at index $j$ equals the block sum of $a$ at $j$: the sum of the $\operatorname{lowbit}(j)$ entries of $a$ ending at position $j - 1$ (positions counted from $0$),…
nodes.title: Fenwick tree representing a list

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
